source.title: Slaying the Hydra: Interaction-Aware Circuit Discovery in Language Models
source.authors: Sankaran Vaidyanathan; R. Urbaniak; Emily Bunnapradist; Michelangelo Naim; Daniel Waxman

page_placements.theme: Compensation and downstream erasure also distort non-ablation attribution, and blocking compensation changes rankings

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures head-level effects with and without witness pinning in GPT-2 IOI, and compares single-head attribution rankings with interaction-aware rankings on circuit outcomes. It refines the self-repair/interaction account but does not directly measure layer-level downstream output restoration.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly reports GPT-2 IOI name-mover and backup effects with and without witnesses (Figure 2), and evaluates circuits selected by different rankings (Table 1). The discussion of layer ablation and self-repair in the introduction cites prior work, so it is not a new result here. The reported faithfulness overshoot concerns circuit-ranking curves, not overshoot of a component’s self-repair effect.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a circuit-discovery method paper (T4-like), but Figure 2 is the study's own result on compensation. In GPT-2 small IOI, pinning downstream 'witness' heads raises the Name Mover group's NIE from 0.14 to 1.16. Scored alone, backups outrank primaries (0.74 vs 0.14). This is a different method (witness pinning) aimed at whether downstream components compensate for a patched head group, and whether single-component scores misstate importance. The circuit-metric comparisons (Table 1) only compare methods and do not test the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors argue that per-component NIE is distorted by interactions such as backup preemption (self-repair), and that witness-integrated, set-level scoring via JuntaLearner yields better circuits. JuntaLearner leads on mean kill and net CRS and matches exact per-head NIE. The benefit of witness pinning is model-dependent, seen mainly on Qwen3.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses witness-integrated set effects and a learned set-ranking procedure, rather than reproducing the original layer-ablation measurement of later-layer self-repair. It evaluates attention-head circuits across task datasets and models.
record.method_sensitivity: Witness pinning has model- and metric-dependent effects: pinning all eligible witnesses lowers all three reported circuit scores on GPT-2 and Llama, while on Qwen3 it improves net and reduces kill and faithfulness. Task, model, witness regime, and ranking objective/configuration vary in the experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Pinning witnesses changes circuit-ranking performance in a model-dependent way. On Qwen3, pinning improves net CRS (+0.7 z) but lowers kill and faithfulness. On GPT-2 and Llama, pinning lowers all three. The authors speculate Qwen3 has many multi-functional backup heads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How much blocking downstream compensation helps circuit discovery varies by model.

fits_no_version.finding: Agreement between per-head NIE rankings and the learned ranking falls as witnesses are held, while WINIE agreement rises (Figure 7, GPT-2 IOI).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Rankings of head importance shift when downstream compensation is blocked.

record.problems: The direct head-level witness evidence is limited to GPT-2 IOI and does not measure general-text output restoration. Main aggregate circuit comparisons summarize fifteen model–task cells without uncertainty values in Table 1; the paper reports seed intervals elsewhere. MIB results use one untuned seed per cell and are not direct evidence about the self-repair mechanism.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported result directly measures the claim’s compensation behavior. The many task-specific circuit curves and MIB comparisons evaluate circuit-ranking performance, not component-level direct versus total effects or downstream restoration.

untested.parts: No whole-layer ablation or measurement of later-layer compensation.
No late-MLP erasure or max-likelihood-token downregulation measured.
No single-head ablation on general text or across model families; the head-group result is GPT-2 small IOI only.
No per-prompt variation or overcorrection of compensation reported. The faithfulness 'overshoot' is a circuit-metric property.

Only backup name movers in GPT-2 IOI. Copy-suppression, LayerNorm rescaling and anti-erasure neurons are not examined, nor is the share of self-repair they explain. Witnesses are generic downstream heads, so the compensation is not isolated to named backups.
No comparison with zero or mean ablation. Only counterfactual-prompt patching is used.
Shown for one head-group comparison in GPT-2 IOI only. No systematic quantification across models or tasks of total vs direct effect.

missing.what: Per-head NIE and witness-integrated values for the individual Name Mover and backup heads (e.g. heads 9.6, 9.9, 10.10, 10.2), including negative values for some heads.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. The only direct self-repair evidence is Figure 2, an illustrative GPT-2 IOI head-group comparison with no uncertainty reported. Rows r3–r5 are method benchmarks and should not carry claim verdicts. The record's V3 link was wrong because IOI is a narrow task. The descriptive discussion of layer ablation cites McGrath et al. and is not a new result.

versions.untested_parts: No layer ablation or later-layer output compensation is measured.
No late-MLP maximum-likelihood-token downregulation or effect of earlier ablations on it is measured.
The reported head-level witness result is limited to GPT-2 IOI; general text, broad prompt coverage, and compensation across model families and sizes are not tested.
Prompt-to-prompt variation and overcorrection of the self-repair effect are not measured. Circuit faithfulness overshoot is a different measure.

The study examines backup name movers in GPT-2 IOI only; it does not test copy-suppression heads, final LayerNorm rescaling, anti-erasure neurons, or how much of self-repair is explained by named mechanisms overall.
No comparison of zero ablation with mean or resample ablation is reported.
The study compares ranking performance on circuit metrics, but does not directly quantify how much a component’s total output effect differs from its direct effect because of downstream compensation.

rows.subject: GPT-2 (IOI circuit)
rows.operation_detail: Compared name-mover effects scored alone by NIE with witness-integrated effects; witnesses are pinned to prevent compensation.
rows.note: The witness-integrated score raises the primary name-mover group above the backups, as the authors describe; it is evidence from one narrow task, not a direct measure of full-output restoration.
rows.check: Wrongly linked to V3: this is a single narrow task (IOI) on one model, not general text across families. The row does bear on V5: the authors attribute the masking to backups ('its backups obscure this role'), though witnesses are all downstream heads, not only backups. It bears on V7: plain NIE understates the primary group (0.14 vs 1.16). It bears on V6: patching uses alternative-prompt (counterfactual) values, an on-distribution intervention. State should be observed, not partial: about 88% of the NM effect is masked.

source_check.locator_found: Section 2, Figure 2 and accompanying Witnesses paragraph: Name Movers NIE 0.14; witness-integrated 1.16.

rows.subject: GPT-2 (IOI circuit)
rows.operation_detail: Compared backup name-mover effects scored alone by NIE with witness-integrated effects; witnesses are pinned to prevent compensation.
rows.note: The backup group’s score is lower with witnesses integrated, while the primary group’s score rises; this identifies a context-dependent backup effect in GPT-2 IOI.
rows.check: Wrongly linked to V3. The backup group's solo NIE (0.74) exceeds the primaries' (0.14), and witness integration reverses the ranking (NM 1.16 > BU 0.60). This is the misranking V7 describes, consistent with backup-head compensation (V5). State should be observed.

source_check.locator_found: Section 2, Figure 2 and accompanying Witnesses paragraph: Backups NIE 0.74; witness-integrated 0.60.

rows.subject: 15 model–task cells (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared circuits formed by the tuned JuntaLearner ranking against circuits formed by signed per-head NIE rankings; circuit heads were patched and kill was summarized by CRS.
rows.note: Aggregate circuit-removal performance is only modestly higher for the interaction-aware ranking than for signed per-head NIE.
rows.check: This compares the study's own method (JuntaLearner) with baselines on Kill CRS. It is method performance, not a measure of self-repair or of attribution error, so it should not be a claim row.

rows.subject: 15 model–task cells (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared circuits formed by the tuned JuntaLearner ranking against circuits formed by signed per-head NIE rankings; circuit heads were patched and faithfulness was summarized by CRS.
rows.note: This circuit-level measure modestly favors the tuned interaction-aware ranking.
rows.check: Own-method vs baseline comparison on Faithfulness CRS; not a measure of the claim.

rows.subject: 15 model–task cells (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared circuits formed by the tuned JuntaLearner ranking against circuits formed by signed per-head NIE rankings; circuit heads were patched and net was summarized by CRS.
rows.note: The tuned interaction-aware ranking has higher aggregate task-specificity scores; this is indirect evidence about attribution rankings, not a direct estimate of downstream restoration.
